kingston-crowned: BHO VCH Surrey vol 3, Kingston: "Edward the Elder was crowned here in 902." "Athelstan in 925, Edmund and Edred in 940 and 946." "In 955 Edwig was elected at a gemot held here and crowned" "In 958 Ethelred 'was very readily and with great joy' crowned here by Dunstan." "All these kings are said to have been crowned on the 'coronation stone' now preserved in the market-place."
Wikipedia, Coronation Stone, Kingston upon Thames: "It is currently located next to the Guildhall in Kingston upon Thames"
tooting-bec: BHO VCH Surrey vol 2, Priory of Tooting: "The name of Tooting Beck or Tooting Bec still preserves the former association ... with the great Benedictine abbey of Bec in Normandy." Grant made "in the life of the Conqueror" by Richard de Tonebridge.
BHO VCH Surrey vol 4, Streatham: "by whom they had been granted before 1086 to the abbey of Bec Hellouin in Normandy."
chapter-house-commons: BHO Old and New London vol 3: "Here, by consent of the then abbot, in 1377, the Commons of England first held their meetings" "here they continued to hold their sittings until 1547."

English Heritage, Chapter House: "the Chapter House saw daily use for the meetings of the Benedictine monks". Note: English Heritage dates the first Commons meeting there to 1352; the card avoids a start year.
aldgate-chaucer: BHO Old and New London vol 2: "Among the records of the City of London is a lease granting the whole of the house above the gate of Aldgate to the poet Chaucer, in 1374."
BHO Memorials of London Life: "Lease to Geoffrey Chaucer of the dwelling-house at Algate." (1374)
Wikipedia, Aldgate: "Aldgate was a gate in the former defensive wall around the City of London." "from 1374 until 1386 ... Geoffrey Chaucer occupied apartments above the gate"
syon-nuns: BHO VCH Middlesex vol 1, Syon Abbey: "The foundation of Syon Abbey at Isleworth in 1415"; Henry V laid the foundation stone "on 22 February 1415"; after the dissolution of the re-established monasteries "The community moved to Flanders, where it began a long exile"; "it continued to exist in Flanders, France, and Portugal"; "its return to England in two groups, one in 1809 and the other in 1861".
fulham-palace: BHO Lysons, Environs vol 2, Fulham: "It is said to have been given to Bishop Erkenwald and his successors, about the year 691"; "The manor-house, or palace of Fulham, has been, from a very early period, the principal summer residence of the Bishops of London."
Historic England, Fulham Palace: "It was the official residence for the Bishop of London until 1973."
greenwich-castle-observatory: BHO Old and New London vol 6: the Observatory "occupies the site of the tower, commonly called 'Greenwich Castle,' which was built by Duke Humphrey"; "The old tower was accordingly ordered to be demolished; and the first stone of the new building was laid in August, 1675"; "constructed in haste, chiefly with the materials of the old tower." Licence for the tower: 1437 (Old and New London vol 6, Greenwich). Card says "a royal duke" rather than naming Humphrey (rule 8).
blackheath-emperor: Wikipedia, Manuel II Palaiologos: "In December 1400, he embarked to England to meet Henry IV of England who received him at Blackheath on the 21st of that month, making him the only Byzantine emperor ever to visit England"; Walsingham: "the Emperor of Constantinople visited England to ask for help against the Turks." Not BHO: Lysons on Eltham doesn't mention the visit.
kew-pagoda-dragons: Wikipedia, Great Pagoda: "80 gilded dragons decorated the roofs of its ten storeys although these had been removed by 1784"; restoration "including the re-carving and reinstatement of the dragons, and its reopening in 2018".
